title: Comparison: Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha

blocks.content: The Lok Sabha represents the people of India as a whole, while the Rajya Sabha represents the states and union territories of India.

rows: Direct election via Universal Adult Suffrage (First-Past-The-Post)
Indirect election by elected MLAs (Single Transferable Vote)
Sole power to introduce and pass Money Bills
Limited to 14 days delay; cannot amend or reject
Speaker (Elected from amongst its own members)
Can be introduced and passed ONLY in Lok Sabha
No power to pass a No-Confidence Motion

items: Rajya Sabha cannot vote on Demands for Grants; this privilege belongs exclusively to the Lok Sabha.
A resolution for the creation of All-India Services under Article 312 can ONLY be originated in the Rajya Sabha by a 2/3rd majority.
The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, but is not a member of either House of Parliament.
Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and require the prior recommendation of the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Lok Sabha is the Lower House directly elected by the people of India, whereas Rajya Sabha is the Upper House indirectly elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.
Lok Sabha has exclusive authority over Money Bills under Article 110; Rajya Sabha can only delay a Money Bill for up to 14 days without power to reject or amend it.
Rajya Sabha is a permanent body not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.
Rajya Sabha possesses exclusive constitutional powers under Article 249 (to authorize legislation on State List) and Article 312 (to create All-India Services).
In a joint sitting of Parliament under Article 108, the Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over the session, giving Lok Sabha numerical superiority.
